2025–26 Topps Chrome Updates Basketball is headlined by one of the most coveted cards in the hobby: Rookie Debut Patch Autographs, making their Topps Basketball debut. Widely regarded as one of The Hobby's premier collectibles, these 1-of-1 grails feature game-worn NBA Debut patches and arrive in basketball for the first time, highlighted by standout rookies Cooper Flagg, Kon Knueppel, and Dylan Harper. The release also showcases superstars including Stephen Curry, LeBron James, Victor Wembanyama, Anthony Edwards, Nikola Jokić, Shai Gilgeous-Alexander, and more across major SSPs and autograph content.
The 200-card base set features refreshed imagery of rookies, veterans, and legends, all presented with updated in-season photography in Statement, City, and Classic Edition uniforms, alongside a deep rainbow of Chrome parallels. Look for new inserts such as New Edition, Stratospheric Stars, No Limit, and Moment in Time, a set that highlights iconic NBA moments like Curry's "Ring Me" celebration in the NBA Finals.
The excitement extends well beyond Rookie Debut Patch Autographs. The release introduces the NBA's first Alter Egos SSPs, an imaginative 10-card set that transforms each player into a dynamic, illustrated, super-powered persona. Minions NBA are SSPs that reimagine NBA stars as Minions in collaboration with Illumination for a fun, highly collectible crossover insert. In addition, look out for the Denim Tears SSP parallel, and newly added Captains, Celebración short print inserts.
Autograph content is equally impressive with a robust lineup of Topps Chrome Autographs, including special appearances from Druski and Spike Lee. The 1980–81 Topps Basketball Autographs deliver another loaded checklist, while the ultra-cool Lava Lamp Rookie Autographs add a groovy twist. Chrome Updates Basketball is a must-have release, bursting with star power, innovation, and true hobby heat.

Discover 2025-26 Topps Chrome Updates Basketball

Date: Jul 30, 2026

2025–26 Topps Chrome Updates Basketball expands the Chrome lineup with updated player photography, rookies in their new NBA uniforms, new team combinations, and one of the release’s biggest new features: Rookie Debut Patch Autographs.

Each one-of-one Rookie Debut Patch Autograph pairs a rookie signature with the NBA Debut patch taken from the jersey worn during that player’s first NBA game. The checklist includes Cooper Flagg, Kon Knueppel, Dylan Harper, Ace Bailey, Cedric Coward, Derik Queen, Egor Demin, and other members of the rookie class.

Collectors can choose from five primary configurations: Hobby, Jumbo, Delight, Value, and Mega. Each format offers a different balance of autographs, parallels, inserts, exclusives, pack volume, and total cards.

Hobby is the best all-around 2025–26 Topps Chrome Updates Basketball box for most collectors. Choose Jumbo when guaranteed autographs are the priority, Delight for a concentrated two-autograph opening, Value for an accessible retail format with exclusive color, or Mega for X-Fractors and a stronger rookie-focused retail experience.

2025-26 Topps Chrome Updates Basketball Hobby Box

A Hobby Box contains 20 packs with four cards per pack and guarantees one autograph.

Hobby’s greatest strength is variety. It delivers the traditional pack-opening experience while offering access to autographs, Refractors, numbered parallels, inserts, and premium short-print cards.

The autograph checklist includes Topps Chrome Autographs, 1980–81 Topps Basketball Autographs, Rookie Lava Lamp Autographs, and special cards featuring personalities such as Druski and Spike Lee.

Collectors can also find inserts including Helix, Alter Egos, Celebración, Captains, and Radiating Rookies. Additional highlights include the Denim Tears SSP parallel and Rookie Debut Patch Autographs.

Who should buy a Hobby Box?

Hobby is the strongest choice for collectors who want to experience the release’s full personality. The 20-pack format provides a satisfying opening for set builders, while the guaranteed autograph and broad card selection give autograph and parallel collectors plenty to explore.

Choose Hobby if you want the most balanced mix of cards, variety, and premium content.

DISCOVER NOW

2025-26 Topps Chrome Updates Basketball Jumbo Box

A Jumbo Box contains 12 packs with 11 cards per pack and guarantees three autographs.

With 132 total cards, Jumbo provides the largest opening experience among the featured configurations. Its defining feature is the three-autograph guarantee, which emphasizes signatures while still providing Refractors, inserts, parallels, and numbered cards.

The autograph lineup can include rookie signatures, current players, legends, and several themed autograph designs. Jumbo therefore gives collectors multiple opportunities to find an important rookie signature or a notable veteran autograph in one box.

Who should buy a Jumbo Box?

Jumbo is designed for autograph collectors, group breakers, and anyone planning a substantial opening. It costs more than a standard Hobby Box, but the three guaranteed autographs make its core value proposition easy to understand.

Choose Jumbo when autographs are your top priority.

DISCOVER NOW

2025-26 Topps Chrome Updates Basketball Delight Box

A Delight Box delivers two autographs in one concentrated pack.

The format centers on Geometric content. Each box includes one Chrome autograph and one Geometric autograph, while the parallel checklist features exclusive Geometric Refractors. The rarest listed versions include White Geometric Refractors numbered to two.

Delight also provides opportunities to find premium inserts such as Captains, Celebración, and Radiating Rookies.

Who should buy a Delight Box?

Delight is best suited to collectors who prefer immediate autograph reveals over a longer pack-opening experience. It is also a natural fit for breakers and parallel specialists interested in the exclusive Geometric designs.

The tradeoff is lower base-card volume than Hobby or Jumbo, so this is not the strongest format for set building.

Release information

This card was included in the Base Set, first released in the Japanese Expansion Pack. A 1st Edition version of this card was included in the 2-Player Starter Set, with the Shadowless variant being available in the first (Shadowless) print of the Set and the non-Shadowless being available in the second print. While an Unlimited Edition version of the Base Set print of this card was never officially released, a Non Holofoil version of this card lacking the 1st Edition stamp was included in the Trainer Deck A, distributed to prototype Pokémon Leagues before the TCG officially launched in North America. Like the rest of the cards included in the deck, this print has a red border and "Trainer Deck A" printed on the back. Another 1st Edition Base Set version of this card, with the Cosmos Holofoil treatment, was included in the 2-Player CD-ROM Starter Set released alongside Base Set 2, which was only released outside of Japan. This card was reprinted in the Legendary Collection expansion, which was also only released outside of Japan.

Trivia

Origin

Strikes Back's Japanese name is that of Counterattack, a skill later introduced in Pokémon Shuffle. Seismic Toss is a move in the Pokémon games that Machamp can learn. This card's English Pokédex entry comes from Pokémon Red and Blue, though it is slightly reworded. The Japanese entry comes from Pokémon Red and Green.

The Machamp is card #8/102 in the 1999 Pokemon Game Base Set (Wizards of the Coast) — the set that launched the Pokemon Trading Card Game. It is a rare holo Fighting-type Stage 2 card, issued across four printings: 1st Edition, Shadowless, Unlimited and the 1999-2000 (4th) print. Across PSA and SGC, roughly 43,689 copies have been graded, with only 448 earning a PSA 10 (Gem Mint) — a sense of how scarce top-grade examples are.

It is a rare holo Fighting-type card and exists in four printings: 1st Edition, Shadowless, Unlimited and the 1999-2000 print.
How can I tell which printing of the Machamp I have?Check three tells: a 1st Edition has the black 'Edition 1' stamp at the lower-left of the artwork; a Shadowless has no stamp AND no drop shadow on the right of the art box (plus an extra '99' in the copyright line); Unlimited has the drop shadow and is by far the most common; the 1999-2000 print looks like Unlimited but its copyright reads (c)1999-2000.
How rare is a graded Machamp?Across PSA and SGC, roughly 43,689 copies of the Machamp have been graded, of which only 448 earned a PSA 10 (Gem Mint). Mid-grade copies are obtainable, but gem-mint examples are genuinely scarce.
Which printing of the Machamp is most valuable?1st Edition copies command the highest premium, followed by Shadowless, with Unlimited the most affordable. See the live per-printing TCGplayer prices above.

Politoed è un Pokémon di tipo Acqua introdotto in seconda generazione.

Si evolve da Poliwhirl quando scambiato mentre tiene una Roccia di re. È una delle evoluzioni finali di Poliwag, l'altra è Poliwrath.

Biologia

Fisionomia

I Politoed sono rane dalla pelle color verde chiaro, tranne la pancia, la mascella, le zampe anteriori e le dita delle zampe posteriori che sono di colore giallo, mentre sulla pancia ha una spirale verde chiaro a indicare la posizione dell'intestino. Il Pokémon ha inoltre le macchie sulle guance di colore rosa, grandi occhi castani e un lungo ciuffo azzurro sulla testa arricciato.

Differenze tra i sessi
Le macchie rosa sulle guance sono più piccole nella femmina.

Abilità speciali

Oltre ad avere le abilità basiche della maggior parte dei Pokémon di tipo Acqua, i Politoed hanno anche la capacità di poter attaccare usando la voce sfruttando mosse come Ultimocanto o Coro. Oltre a questo possiedono una grande capacità di salto. Anche se fisicamente sono più deboli dei Poliwrath, sono più forti quando attaccano specialmente.

Comportamento

I Politoed sono spesso a capo dei branchi di Poliwag, Poliwhirl e talvolta anche Poliwrath, che loro richiameranno con il loro gracchiare, nel caso in cui si dovessero incontrare due Politoed, il leader verrà deciso dal gracchiare. Nonostante ciò sono anche astuti predatori e sfruttano la loro lunga lingua per catturare gli insetti, possono inoltre sfruttare il ciuffo sulla testa per mimetizzarsi fra le alghe.

Habitat

I Politoed sono estremamente rari in natura in quanto un Poliwhirl necessità dell'intervento dell'uomo per evolversi, tuttavia loro vivono nei laghi e negli stagni, li si può vedere sopra delle foglie di ninfea.

Dieta

Articolo principale: Cibo Pokémon
I Politoed non solo assorbono sostanze nutritive dell'acqua tramite la pelle, ma possono anche cacciare Pokémon insetto con la loro lingua lunga e appiccicosa.

Inserting the Batteries into the Remote
The remote may have a screw that secures the battery 
compartment cover onto the remote control (or this may 
be in a separate bag). Remove the screw, if the cover 
is screwed on previously. Then remove the battery 
compartment cover to reveal the battery compartment. 
Insert two 1.5V - size AAA batteries. Make sure the (+) 
and (-) signs match (observing correct polarity). Do not 
mix old and new batteries. Replace only with same or 
equivalent type. Place the cover back on. Secure the 
cover again with the screw, if any.
Standby Button
Press and hold the Standby button on the remote 
control. Power off dialogue will appear on the screen. 
Highlight OK and press the OK button. The TV will 
switch into standby mode. Press briefly and release 
to switch the TV into quick standby mode or to switch 
on the TV when in quick standby or standby mode.
1. Standby: Quick Standby / Standby / On
2. Numeric buttons: Switches the channel in Live TV 
mode, enters a number in the text box on the screen
3. Language: Switches among sound modes (analogue 
TV), displays and changes audio language (digital TV, 
where available)
4. Mute: Completely turns off the volume of the TV
5. Volume +/-: Increases/decreases the volume level
6. Guide: Displays the electronic programme guide for 
Live TV channels
7. Directional buttons: Navigates menus, setting options, 
moves the focus or cursor, etc.
